messages:
Sam: Quick question — customer (UK healthcare) wants to lock traffic to eu-west-2 only and ensure no US sub‑processors for inference. They also want a POC to validate latency. Can we confirm what routing options we can offer for a hosted vs dedicated setup? Also they'll want pricing delta if we guarantee region affinity.

Anna (PS): We can do region affinity policies. For hosted, we can route by tenant->region preference but not strict hard isolation (soft-affinity + failover). For Dedicated you can get strict isolation (pinned capacity in a region). Pricing-wise, dedicated is a monthly commit; I can sketch numbers if you share expected qps and token volume.

Sam: Thanks. They asked for an example policy snippet we could show them for the POC — something they can use to verify requests stay in eu-west-2 and fall back to eu-west-1 only if capacity is exhausted.

Michael (Infra): Example policy (very simplified):
```
routing_policy: 
  - tenant: customer-acme
    preferred_regions: [eu-west-2]
    fallback_regions: [eu-west-1]
    hard_isolation: false  # hosted: false, dedicated/private: true
```
Notes: hosted uses affinity cookies and region tags — we don't guarantee circuit-level enforcement unless you use Dedicated/Private. Also call out that some control-plane operations (billing, scheduler) may touch US infra depending on contract — ask privacy/legal if they need absolute attestations.

Sam: That's helpful. Any sub‑processor list to send to customer? They specifically asked about model storage and telemetry endpoints.

PrivacyBot: Subprocessor summary (short):
- Model storage: BlobStore EU (primary), backup in US for hosted (can be disabled with Dedicated/Private)
- Telemetry/analytics: EU for customers with EU residency add-on; default routed to analytics.redwood.ai (US)
- Support tools (SaaS): may be third‑party (Zendesk/Datadog) — we can provide subprocessor agreement and SOC docs.

Anna (PS): If they need no US touch at all we should propose Redwood Private (VPC or on‑prem). For the POC we can also set a contract addendum to limit backups to EU for the trial window — need legal signoff.

Ian: For the POC, to validate latency we usually deploy a small dedicated pool in eu-west-2 (g4dn-like) and provide a test token+simple harness. We can also enable prefix KV caching to reduce tail latency. Expected lead time ~ 7 business days for provisioning.

Sam: Perfect. I'll ask for qps and token estimates. Can someone drop the subprocessor link and a short blurb I can paste into the security questionnaire?

Michael (Infra): Link: https://redwood.ai/legal/subprocessors (send as reference). Blurb you can paste: "Redwood routes customer inference requests to the specified region according to routing policies. For hosted deployments, non-customer-managed control-plane components and optional backups may transit certified subprocessors outside the EU unless a residency add-on, Dedicated, or Private deployment is in place. We provide SOC2 and DPA addenda on request."

Anna (PS): I'll stand by to model pricing once Sam shares volumes. If they want a hard no-US guarantee for the POC, escalate to Private + legal addendum.

Sam: Thanks everyone :thumbsup: — I'll get the numbers and update the thread.
